title: Soundness of the relativised safe-recursion function algebras: the permutation-of-prefixes algebra captures polynomial time and the nested algebra captures elementary computation
author: Gianluca Curzi; Anupam Das
difficulty_reason: After the paper's relativised Bounding Lemma (Lemma 41) and the definitions of the algebras B, B^{pp}, NB and NB^{pp} are in place, the counted theorem still needs a paper-specific simulation argument. Soundness is proved by induction on the definition of f: the initial functions are polynomial time and the schemes are handled one by one, with each oracle call replaced by an explicitly bounded function computing its graph via the Bounding Lemma; the recursion case is then evaluated by a course-of-values recursion along the permutation-of-prefixes order whose lookup table must be shown to have polynomial size, using the m! permutations of the prefixes of a list and a bound on the growth rate, with the nested/elementary case requiring a separate argument because the safe inputs of recursive calls must be bounded before the table can be stored. Establishing that a circular, two-tiered proof system only defines functions of the intended complexity is research-level implicit computational complexity, not a qualifying-exam recurrence exercise.
